correctness.rationale: With distances recomputed, uniqueness of joins removes only the point pairs involving p on faulted lines; the restriction to points is the union of two simplices along a nonempty simplex since at least one incidence survives. The restriction to lines is a cone at any line outside the pencil. Parity and the absence of four-cycles force every mixed clique to have a singleton on one shore. The two resulting pieces collapse to their contractible shore complexes and intersect in the connected faulted graph. The homotopy pushout is its suspension, with cycle rank (q+1)(q²+q+1)−t−2(q²+q+1)+1=q³−t. Natural Mayer–Vietoris gives inclusion of integral graph cycles. In the larger graph a spanning tree of the smaller one gives a fundamental cycle projecting to each newly missing edge coordinate, so the quotient is freely Z^(t−s). At t=q the leaf p is dominated in the flag complex by its unique remaining line; a leaf cannot shorten distances between remaining vertices, giving the asserted strong collapse onto exactly the punctured-graph complex. These arguments also apply at q=2 and t=0.
residual_risks: Recorded checks of PG(2,2) and PG(2,3) are finite binary checks of the absolute complexes, not integral map proofs. The independent conclusion uses the plane axioms and the cycle-lattice argument, not an execution of the packaged script.
